Divisibility of Separated Polynomials

A criterion explaining when divisibility of two-variable polynomial differences forces composition with a common one-variable polynomial.

The argument uses a residue expansion in a free module, followed by a reduction along the diagonal. A companion exposition revisits the same criterion through Galois theory and Frobenius descent.

Background

Polynomial rings and basic field theory.

Read the full exposition

The complete argument is available as a PDF.

Revision history · September 22, 2026

Revised September 22, 2026: added a full fiber-constancy criterion over arbitrary fields, using Hasse derivatives to retain inseparable multiplicities. The original composition theorem and its free-module proof are unchanged. The PDF and TeX source agree.
